property_summary: For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId if it returns true for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, but the mutant fails to recognize IERC1155 even when it recognizes IERC1155MetadataURI.
For any interfaceId input, if supportsInterface returns true, then it must also return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId when the input is type(IERC1155).interfaceId.

For any valid interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, then it must also return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId, but the mutant fails to recognize IERC1155.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return the same value for type(IERC1155).interfaceId and type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false for IERC1155 while returning true for IERC1155MetadataURI.

For any token that inherits ERC1155, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId and type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, but the buggy version only returns true for type(IERC165).interfaceId.
The reference contract correctly reports support for IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI via supportsInterface, while the buggy mutant only reports support for IERC165.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract returns the correct supported status while the mutant returns false for IERC1155/IERC1155MetadataURI interfaces, violating the expected interface reporting.

For any interface ID that is neither type(IERC165).interfaceId nor the zero interface, both C and the mutant should return false; however, for type(IERC1155).interfaceId and type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId the reference returns true while the mutant incorrectly returns false.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true exactly when interfaceId matches the IERC165, IERC1155, or IERC1155MetadataURI interface ids; the mutant breaks this by returning false for the latter two.

The supportsInterface function should return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId, but the buggy version mistakenly uses type(IERC20).interfaceId instead, causing it to return false for the actual ERC1155 interface.
The supportsInterface function must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId in the reference contract, but returns false in the buggy contract because the mutant replaces IERC1155 with IERC20.
The supportsInterface function must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the buggy version returns false because it checks for type(IERC20).interfaceId instead.
supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant checks type(IERC20).interfaceId instead, causing it to return false for the actual ERC1155 interface.

For any bytes4 selector, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC1155).interfaceId; the mutant replaces the check with type(IERC20).interfaceId, making it return false for the actual ERC1155 interface.

For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface returns true if and only if one of the expected IERC1155 or IERC1155MetadataURI interfaces is queried; the bug incorrectly returns true for the IERC20 interfaceId, violating the contract's declared interface support.

For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface returns true only for type(IERC1155).interfaceId or type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId; the bug returns true also for type(IERC20).interfaceId, which violates the contract's declared interface support.

For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface conforms exactly to IERC165: it returns true for IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI, but false for all other interfaceIds; the bug wrongly returns true for type(IERC20).interfaceId, breaking the invariant that it must not report unsupported interfaces.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return the same result as the canonical reference implementation ERC1155.supportsInterface(interfaceId), but the buggy version returns true for type(IERC20).interfaceId where it should return false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return the same boolean as the unimpeachable reference logic (type(IERC1155).interfaceId, type(IERC1155MetadataURI).interfaceId, or super.supportsInterface); the buggy version returns true for type(IERC20).interfaceId, violating this equivalence.
For any account and token id, the balanceOf call must revert when the account is the zero address, but the mutant returns 0 instead.

For any account and token id, the return value of balanceOf must equal the internal _balances storage mapping entry, but the mutant returns 0 when account is address(0) instead of reverting with the original require message.

For any account and any token id, if balanceOf does not revert, the returned balance must equal the internal _balances[id][account], but the mutant returns 0 when account is address(0) while the original reverts.
For any account and token id, balanceOf(account, id) must not revert when account is not address(0), and the mutant must return a different value than the original for address(0).
